attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses this assessment in his own article, referring to himself in the third person.

semantics.note: Faithful on the contextual reading of unreliable factual discrimination by contemporary LLMs, rather than absolute inability or a claim about all future models.

contract.note: The practical reliability reading is ordinary given the surrounding discussion. The contract fairly admits successful checking methods and distinguishes factual errors from source unfaithfulness.

evidence.note: The May 2023 evaluation directly tests recognition and reports substantial recurring errors, including with retrieval. Summarization findings require caution because unsupported content can be factually true.

Recognition of many previously generated errors is material counterevidence to absolute inability. Conditional detection rates on three constructed tasks do not establish dependable general factual checking.

Successful repeated-sampling checks qualify the claim. Biographical passage results and ranking metrics do not establish dependable classification across varied factual tasks. Publication predates the cutoff.

reviews.rationale: Under the fair practical reliability reading, direct recognition evaluations show substantial recurring failures in contemporary models. Successful separate checking and repeated sampling demonstrate useful capabilities, but their limited tasks and metrics do not establish dependable general factual discrimination. The evidence supports unreliability, not complete inability.
